Entries.Text: Write every edited clip into its anibnd in the project. The character is read again afterwards, so the undo history is cleared.
No character in this project has an anibnd.
{0} has no animations this editor can read.
Failed to open the animations of {0}
{0} has edited clips that aren't saved. Opening {1} drops them unless they are saved first.
Select a character to list its clips.
Plays the animations of {0}. Saving edits them for every character that shares them.
Copy this clip, as it is now, under a new ID in the same anibnd. Listed as (new) until saved. Can be undone.
The name of the copy of {0} (aXXX_YYYYYY):
Move this clip to another ID. On save, the file is written under the new ID and the old one is taken out of the anibnd. Time acts and behaviors that use the old ID are not changed. Can be undone.
Take this clip out of its anibnd on save. Time acts and behaviors that use it are not changed. Can be undone.
Select a clip to play and edit it.
{0} can't be decoded by this editor.
The selected clip. Edits play in the viewport straight away and are written to the anibnd when saved.
Additive: played on top of another animation
One frame back (Left Arrow while the Timeline is focused)
One frame on (Right Arrow while the Timeline is focused)
Play or pause the clip in the viewport (Space while the Timeline is focused). Root motion isn't applied: the character plays in place.
How fast the clip plays in the viewport. This doesn't change the clip: use Speed in the Clip tool for that.
Frame {0}. Click or drag to go there. Yellow marks are the selected bone's keys, grey ones other bones' keys.
The bones of {0}'s model couldn't be read, so the clip can't be shown on it.
Each operation makes a new version of the clip, which can be undone. Root motion is edited with the poses.
Keep only the frames from First to Last (both kept). The root motion starts from zero again at the new first frame.

Play the clip faster or slower: 2 is twice as fast (half the frames), 0.5 half as fast. The root covers the same distance in the new time.

Time act events keep their times, so they may need moving in the Time Act Editor.
A bone turns {0} degrees between two frames of this clip. At this speed that becomes {1} degrees, past 180, so it would turn the short way round (a fast spin would go backwards).
Play the clip over this many frames, at the same frame rate. The same as Speed, given as a length.
Play the clip backwards. The root goes back along its path from where the clip ended.
Swap the character's left and right sides: each L_ bone takes its R_ bone's motion, mirrored, and the other way round. The root turns the other way.
An additive clip can't be mirrored.
{0} animated bones have a mirror bone this clip doesn't animate, so their motion is lost when mirrored. Hover to see them.
More clips match: filter to find one.
Play the picked clip after this one. Over the blend frames, the end of this clip crossfades into the start of the picked one, and the root carries on from where this clip left it.
The picked clip doesn't animate the same bones in the same order, so it can't be appended.
The picked clip has different float tracks, so it can't be appended.
One clip is additive and the other isn't, so they can't be joined.
Drop this clip's edits, back to its file as saved. Can be undone.
How opaque the character's mesh is drawn. Lower it to see the skeleton through the body. Only the viewport is affected.
Draw the clip's root motion path (green): where the root goes over the clip from the origin, a mark each second, and an arrow at the playing frame showing where the character faces.
Move the character along its root motion while it plays, as the game does, instead of playing in place. The skeleton, bone picking and the gizmo follow it.
This clip has no root motion: the game doesn't move the character while it plays. Add it below.

For a clip whose character moves away from where it starts by moving its root bone: that travel becomes root motion, and the bone keeps the rest. With the root motion applied (in game, or Display > Travel) the character looks the same, but the game now moves it.
No bone can give root motion: it needs an animated bone whose parents the clip doesn't animate (normally Master).
The bone whose travel becomes root motion. Master, the skeleton's root, moves the whole character.
The bone's turn about up becomes root motion too, so the game turns the character.
The bone's up and down movement becomes root motion too (a jump). Off, it stays in the bone and the root stays on the ground.
Move the bone's travel into root motion. Can be undone.
For a clip that plays in place: how far the game moves and turns the character over the clip. The poses don't change, so the character slides unless the clip was made to travel.
How far the character travels the way it faces, over the whole clip. Negative goes backwards.
How far the character travels to its right. Negative goes left.
How far the character rises (negative: falls) over the clip.
How far the character turns over the clip, in degrees. Positive turns right, negative left.
Linear travels at an even speed; Smooth starts and ends gently.
Give the clip this root motion. Can be undone.
Root motion path for {0} ({1} forward, {2} deg turn)
How far the clip moves the character by its last frame.
Multiply each part of the root motion. The poses stay as they are, so a large change makes the feet slide.
How far the character travels along the ground, times this: 1.2 makes a lunge go a fifth further, 0 keeps it in place.
How far the character moves up or down, times this: 0 keeps it on the ground.
How far the character turns, times this: 0 keeps its facing, -1 turns it the other way.
Scale the root motion by the three values. Can be undone.
Common root motion changes in one click, each undoable.
Remove the up and down part of the root motion, keeping the character on the ground.
Keep the character facing the way it started, while still travelling.
The clip plays in place: the character doesn't move or turn while it plays.
The path is drawn in the viewport (Display > Show Root Path); Display > Travel moves the character along it while playing.
Scale root motion of {0} (ground x{1}, vertical x{2}, turn x{3})
How large the joint spheres are drawn, times their default (a hundredth of the skeleton's height). Clicking a joint selects its bone.
{0} offset keys on {1} bones (applied when played, saved or given an operation)
Select a bone to move or turn it in the viewport.
The selected bone. The viewport gizmo is on it, at the playing frame.
This clip doesn't animate this bone, so it can't be keyed: a clip only animates the bones its binding lists.

Drag the gizmo in the viewport to move or turn this bone at the playing frame (Move or Rotate below), or type the offset in the fields. Each drag or Apply adds or changes the key at that frame. One key moves the bone for the whole clip; a zero key on each side limits it to a range.
Set the viewport gizmo to {0} ({1} while the viewport or this window is focused).
How far the bone is turned from the clip's own pose at this frame, in degrees about its parent's X, then Y, then Z axis.
How far the bone is moved from the clip's own pose at this frame, along its parent's X, Y and Z axes.
Set these as the key at this frame (adding the key if there is none). Can be undone.
Fill the fields again with the bone's offset at this frame, dropping what was typed.
How every bone's offset goes from one key to the next in this clip.
Add a key with no offset at the playing frame, so the bone is as the clip has it there. Put one on each side of a key to limit its effect to that range.
Make a new animation from this clip as it is now, saved next to it in the same anibnd. The original keeps its own ID and content.
Add the clip under this name (aXXX_YYYYYY), listed as (new) until saved. Can be undone.
A clip's name is aXXX_YYYYYY, such as a000_003500.
{0} is already a clip of this character.
A new ID also needs a time act entry (Time Act Editor) for its events, and a behavior clip for the game to play it.
Open the Behavior Editor's Register dialog for this clip's ID, to add the clip generator the game plays it through. The Behavior Editor saves its own file.
{0} couldn't be read, so its clips weren't saved.
{0} isn't in {1} any more, so it wasn't saved.
